title: Trump’s Russia deals are not his to make – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: ECFR argues that Trump's offers to Moscow (frozen reserves, Lukoil and Nord Stream asset sales, Russian diesel imports, sanctions waivers) depend on assets and law located in the EU, so EU governments can veto or shape them. It proposes EU approval of Russian energy-asset sales, a firm Russian-gas phase-out date, and a claims-offset counter-proposal on reserves.

insights.claim: US envoys offered Moscow access to part of the roughly $300bn of immobilised Russian central-bank reserves and a Lukoil foreign-business sale to investors close to the envoys, while Trump let US firms import Russian diesel and waived part of the new Graham act sanctions.
insights.speaker: Agathe Demarais, Jim O’Brien
entities: Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act
insights.so_what: Signals US sanctions relief on Russian energy is being traded; watch Lukoil asset sales and diesel flows.
insights.locator: Donald Trump is in a giving mood

insights.claim: Many of the concessions Trump offers Russia are not Washington's to give, because the assets, sanctions regulation and legal custody sit in the EU.
insights.speaker: Agathe Demarais, Jim O’Brien
insights.so_what: EU legal control of the assets caps the value of any US-Russia deal to buyers.
insights.quote: many of the things that Trump is offering Moscow are not Washington’s to give

insights.claim: Euroclear in Belgium holds the bulk of the roughly $300bn of immobilised Russian reserves, and only EU governments can amend the regulation keeping that money under EU jurisdiction.
insights.speaker: Agathe Demarais, Jim O’Brien
insights.so_what: Reserve release requires EU action; a US-brokered release is not executable alone.

insights.claim: Lukoil's foreign assets sit largely on EU soil (Burgas in Bulgaria, Petrotel in Romania, a Zeeland refinery stake in the Netherlands, Teboil in Finland), and Gazprom holds 51% of Nord Stream alongside German, French and Dutch shareholders, giving the EU a hold over any sale.
insights.speaker: Agathe Demarais, Jim O’Brien
insights.so_what: Buyers of these assets face EU legal and screening risk even with US blessing.

insights.claim: Lukoil is on the US sanctions list but not the EU's, and EU sanctions do not stop Gazprom selling its Nord Stream stake to an American buyer, so Europe currently looks like a bystander.
insights.speaker: Agathe Demarais, Jim O’Brien
insights.so_what: Near-term the gap lets US-approved deals proceed unless the EU closes it.
insights.locator: On paper, Europe looks like a bystander

insights.claim: Gazprom Neft cut its stake in Serbian refiner NIS to just under the 50% threshold that would trigger EU sanctions, so NIS escapes EU measures and the US Treasury sets every sale deadline.
insights.speaker: Agathe Demarais, Jim O’Brien
insights.so_what: NIS ownership outcome is being set by Washington; watch for an EU control review.
insights.locator: The fate of Serbian refiner NIS

insights.claim: The EU should require its own approval for sales of Russian-owned energy assets on EU territory, conditioned on Russian concessions rather than American participation, via Council sanctions on Lukoil with a licence mirroring the US one, a Commission review of NIS control, and co-ordinated national investment screening.
insights.speaker: Agathe Demarais, Jim O’Brien
insights.so_what: Raises regulatory risk for any Lukoil or Nord Stream transaction; watch the next EU sanctions package.

insights.claim: Nord Stream's value to a US buyer depends on EU gas policy: with Russian pipeline gas imports to end by September 2027 the stake has no customers, but Slovakia and Hungary asked on October 19th for flexibility and far-right gains plus France's spring 2027 election raise delay risk.
insights.speaker: Agathe Demarais, Jim O’Brien
insights.so_what: A slipped ban date is the key variable for European gas pricing and Nord Stream optionality.

insights.claim: The EU should counter Washington on reserves by netting claims: Ukraine reconstruction needs of $588bn (World Bank, February 2026) plus over $170bn of Western corporate losses in Russia imply Russian liabilities of more than twice its immobilised assets.
insights.speaker: Agathe Demarais, Jim O’Brien
insights.so_what: Frames reserves as collateral for reparations, reducing odds of release back to Russia.

insights.claim: Resisting Trump carries costs such as tariff threats on buyers of Russian energy, but Trump's concessions face domestic opposition and a Democratic House could trigger investigations into the insider-linked deals.
insights.speaker: Agathe Demarais, Jim O’Brien
insights.so_what: US political risk to the Lukoil and Nord Stream deals rises after the midterms.

insights.claim: US-friendly buyers of Russian assets are not safer than Moscow-connected ones, since they could resell to well-connected Russians, and a sale that sends funds to Russia defeats the purpose of sanctions.
insights.speaker: Agathe Demarais, Jim O’Brien
insights.so_what: Challenges the premise that Western ownership neutralises sanctions risk.
